# ResQueue — Android (Trusted Web Activity)

This wraps the ResQueue PWA (`/mobile`) in a Trusted Web Activity (TWA) — a
thin native Android shell that renders your live site full-screen via
Chrome's engine. It's Google's official, supported path for shipping a PWA
to Play Store, not a workaround.

**This project was hand-authored** (not generated by the `bubblewrap` CLI —
that tool insists on an interactive JDK-install prompt that doesn't work in
a non-interactive shell). It follows the same structure Bubblewrap would
produce, so `bubblewrap build` will also work against `twa-manifest.json`
if you get the CLI running locally later.

## Before you can build this

1. **Android Studio** (bundles its own JDK — you don't need to install one
   separately). https://developer.android.com/studio
2. **A real, publicly reachable HTTPS domain** serving ResQueue. A TWA
   cannot verify against an IP address or `localhost` — the deployment
   guide from earlier (systemd + nginx + Let's Encrypt on your EC2 box,
   see `../deploy/`) gets you this.

## Steps

### 1. Choose your package ID and domain

Two placeholders are used everywhere below — replace all of them:
- `com.resqueue.app` → your real package ID (permanent once you publish;
  can't be changed later). Reverse-DNS, ideally under a domain you own.
- `resqueue.example.com` → your real deployed domain.

Files to update: `app/build.gradle` (`applicationId` and `namespace`),
`app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml` (`hostName`, `launchUrl`,
`asset_statements`), `twa-manifest.json`.

### 2. Open in Android Studio

File → Open → select this `android-twa/` folder. Let Gradle sync (it will
download the Android Gradle Plugin and the `androidbrowserhelper`
dependency — this needs internet access once, then it's cached).

### 3. Create a signing key

You need this once, and **must keep it forever** — losing it means you can
never publish an update to the same app listing again.

```bash
keytool -genkeypair -v -keystore android.keystore -alias android \
  -keyalg RSA -keysize 2048 -validity 10000
```

Get its SHA-256 fingerprint (you'll need this for step 4):

```bash
keytool -list -v -keystore android.keystore -alias android
```

Copy the line starting `SHA256:`.

### 4. Verify domain ownership (Digital Asset Links)

Put that SHA-256 fingerprint and your real package ID into
`../static/assetlinks.json` (already wired up — the Flask server serves it
at `/.well-known/assetlinks.json`, which is where Android looks for it).
Redeploy the server so that file is live over HTTPS before you test the
installed app — without it, links open in a browser tab instead of the
app's own window (the TWA still installs and runs, it just won't feel
fully "native" until this is in place).

### 5. Build a release bundle

```bash
./gradlew bundleRelease \
  -PRESQUEUE_KEYSTORE=../android.keystore \
  -PRESQUEUE_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD=<your password> \
  -PRESQUEUE_KEY_ALIAS=android \
  -PRESQUEUE_KEY_PASSWORD=<your password>
```

This produces `app/build/outputs/bundle/release/app-release.aab` — the
file Play Console wants (not an APK).

### 6. Play Console

Needs your own **Google Play Developer account** ($25 one-time,
https://play.google.com/console/signup) — this is tied to your identity
and payment, so it's not something that can be done on your behalf.

- Create the app, upload `app-release.aab` under Production (or start with
  Internal Testing to try it privately first).
- Store listing needs: app icon (512×512, already generated at
  `store-assets/play-store-icon-512.png`), at least 2 phone screenshots
  (take these from the running `/mobile` app — annotate/crop as needed),
  a short + full description, and a **privacy policy URL** (required
  because ResQueue collects email addresses and passwords — even a simple
  one-page policy hosted anywhere works, it just needs to be a real
  reachable URL).
- Fill out the **Data safety** questionnaire — declare that you collect
  email address (account creation) and that it's not shared with third
  parties, no ads/analytics unless you add them later.
- First submission typically takes a few hours to a few days for Google's
  review.

## What this is NOT

This doesn't touch anything in the Flask app's business logic — the TWA is
just a native shell pointing at your existing `/mobile` page. Every screen,
API call, and feature works identically to visiting the URL directly; the
only difference is it opens without browser chrome and has a launcher icon.
